findings.title: "Verified graph facts" and 943 references are not verifiable against the project state
findings.description: The design states the facts were "Probed against this repo's real graph … while writing this design" and that "These are measurements, not assumptions." The repository contradicts that premise: slice 361's own design and task files carry `status: not_started`; the 361 entry in the slice plan is unchecked; `361-tasks.graph-contract-and-provenance.md` (frontmatter `projectState`) says "No graph exists in this repo yet"; there is no `.understand-anything/` directory in the repo, no `user/analysis/943-analysis.codebase-comprehension.md` (only 940–942 exist), no `commands/analysis/understand.md` (the 361 deliverable), and no 361 branch (only `main` exists). Consequently: (a) the specific numbers in the table (925 nodes / 2184 edges / hash `1bfbca1`, the 238 reconciliation) cannot be confirmed as measurements; (b) the claims "The generated `943` sample carries both wrong counts" (line 136), "943 exists, so expect **944**" (line 368), and "The 943 document generated during slice 361 carries the two wrong layer counts" (line 468) reference an artifact that does not exist; (c) Verification Walkthrough step 1 is worded as re-verification ("re-run them, because the graph may have been refreshed"), not as a first-time measurement gate — if the graph does not yet exist, the jq commands fail rather than "not agreeing." The requirement left unmet: design decisions that rest on measurements (both corrections, the 238-node coverage arithmetic) must be verifiable. Fix: restate the premise — mark 361 completion as a hard precondition of this slice, present the facts as pending verification (or reword as "expected values to confirm"), make step 1 an explicit gate that stops if `.understand-anything/` is absent, and correct the 943/944 index expectation (the corrected run would produce 943, not 944, if 361's proving run happens under 361's own walkthrough).

findings.title: Extraction mapping and sections align with the architecture's comprehension output
findings.description: The architecture's capability-(a) output for the comprehension document is "layers, complexity hotspots, entry points, dependency observations"; all four are present in the seven-section mapping, each with named source fields, an ordering rule, and a binding fallback (sourced content or `[GAP: ...]`, no third option) — consistent with the architecture's "never fabricate intent" goal and the `[INFERRED]` governance decision, which matches 361's stated handoff ("362 governs its use in the deepened analysis"). The two absorbed open questions are handled as assigned: gap markers inherit 361's settled syntax, and the `analyze-codebase-prompt.md` reuse decision retains the document as required ("Prior art (retained, not superseded)") with only a one-line cross-reference. Integration direction matches the slice plan: consumes the 361 preflight/provenance/index conventions unchanged, provides the mapping to 363 (extract-then-ask per-section fields) and the corrected layer/file-level definitions to 364 (whose candidate signals would be wrong under the 361 undercount), and explicitly excludes 363/364/366 scope. The read-discipline requirement is restated with concrete targets (field-scoped `jq` only, 238 in-scope nodes, 687 function/class nodes excluded, success criterion 9), and the observed `config.json` drift (`autoUpdate` absent) is handled correctly by reporting present settings rather than asserting expected keys.

findings.title: Corrections and new reads are proportionate to the slice's mandate
findings.description: No Python, no new files, no installer/manifest/`src/` changes — bounded to `understand.md` plus one cross-reference line, matching the plan's "No Python is added by any slice" invariant. The two corrections to 361's skill text go beyond the literal 362 plan entry but are justified: they fix defect behavior (undercounting layer composition, silently dropping 37 analyzed files) that would otherwise corrupt this slice's coverage arithmetic and slice 364's candidate derivations; they keep a cross-check (nodeIds must resolve to `filePath`-carrying nodes; drift reported, not filtered) so the single-graph measurement is safe on unmeasured graphs; and the implementation order applies them in isolation first with a re-run. Walkthroughs 1, 5, and 6 cover the new I/O paths' failure modes (missing `meta.json`, empty `tour`, no `entry-point` tag, `analyzedFiles` mismatch reporting both numbers) with explicit strategies rather than TBDs. The instruction to leave the 943 document un-edited correctly follows the independent-samples convention.

findings.title: "361 explicitly deferred" traces to the 361 tasks file, not the 361 design
findings.description: The claim that 361 "explicitly deferred" `config.json`, `.understandignore`, and `meta.json`'s `analyzedFiles` is accurate but is documented in `project-documents/user/tasks/361-tasks.graph-contract-and-provenance.md:72-76` (F011/F012 dispositions of review notes), not in the 361 slice design, which never mentions deferring these fields. A reader verifying the premise against the 361 design alone will not find it. Consider naming the F011/F012 dispositions in the 362 design so the deferral chain is auditable without the (not present in the repo) 361 review document.

findings.title: File-level definition now diverges from the architecture's nine-type enumeration
findings.description: Correction 2 deliberately replaces the architecture's nine-type allow-list (`file`, `config`, …, `resource`) with an exclusion rule (`type != "function" and .type != "class"`), with a stated rationale (a tenth upstream file-level type is included automatically rather than silently dropped) and a drift check (filter survivor without `filePath` is reported). The deviation is well-reasoned and stays within the architecture's intent (function/class nodes never read), so it is not a violation — but the architecture's Read-discipline paragraph still presents the nine types as the operative definition, and slices 363/364 will reuse 362's "file-level" definition. A one-line update to the architecture's read-discipline text (operating definition: "all node types except function and class, each must carry `filePath`") would give the initiative a single source of truth.
